Hi Clara — thanks for the questionnaire and the timeline. Below are concise answers aimed at the hosted API configuration that Clearwater trialed (default account settings). I've attached a one-page Data Lifecycle summary and a small curl example for our deletion endpoint.

1) Data residency (where data is stored)
- Default: API request payloads and short-term artifacts for Clearwater trial are stored in the us-west-2 region (multi-AZ) by default.
- Customer option: You can request a pinned region (us-west-2, us-east-1, europe-west1) at account provisioning. For enterprise Private deployments we provide VPC-hosted control plane options.
- Subprocessors: primary object storage and compute are run on AWS in the selected region; we may use GCP/Azure for optional telemetry or analytics in the same region. Subprocessor list and locations are in our SOC2 attachments on the vendor page.

2) Retention windows (defaults & derived artifacts)
- Request payloads (transient cache): persisted for up to 30 days by default for improved latency and to enable debugging.
- Model inputs/outputs for the hosted API (generation tokens, chat logs): retained 30 days by default.
- Embeddings/derived vectors: retained 90 days by default unless explicitly stored by the customer via export.
- Operational logs (audit, request metadata): retained 180 days for troubleshooting and compliance auditability. Access is role-restricted to a small ops and security team.

3) Deletion / erasure process and SLA
- Self-service: Customers can call our Deletion API (endpoint example attached) to request immediate deletion of the account-level request logs and cached artifacts. Typical API processing is asynchronous but completion is usually within 24–72 hours depending on work queue and whether data is present in backups.
- Support-assisted: For legal holds or contract-triggered erasure, file a support ticket via the Redwood Console; our Data Protection team manages the workflow and provides a certified deletion attestation. Standard target for attestation delivery is 5 business days for hosted accounts.
- Note: Deleting data removes it from primary storage and searchable caches; snapshot/backups are then scheduled for purge in the next backup retention cycle (see backups section).

4) Backups & disaster recovery copies
- Backups: We take encrypted backups for operational resilience. Backup retention is 90 days for the hosted offering by default. Backup deletion follows the normal lifecycle; after a deletion request, backups containing the deleted records are truncated/purged according to the backup retention schedule — typically within the next 30 days.
- DR: DR replicas are region-specific; for accounts pinned to a region we do not replicate cross-region unless explicitly enabled for resilience.

5) Encryption and key management
- All data in transit is encrypted via TLS 1.2+; at rest encryption uses AES-256.
- Customer-managed keys: We support KMS integration / BYOK for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted accounts, we offer a customer-managed-key (CMK) option via AWS KMS for an additional compliance add-on — we can scope this into the contract.

6) Access controls and auditability
- Role-based access for all internal tooling; Dynamo/obj-store admin accounts are tightly scoped and audited.
- Audit logs for privilege escalation and data access are retained per the operational logs retention above.

7) Legal holds and exceptional requests
- We can implement legal hold or extended retention on a per-account basis; this is tracked via a change ticket and requires sign-off from the account owner and security.

Hi Clara — quick clarifications below (and I attached a current subprocessors.csv and our SOC2-excerpt PDF).

1) Backup worst-case window
- Operational worst-case: backups and snapshots are retained 90 days by default. In exceptional situations (e.g., long-term DR archives for certain enterprise customers) that may be extended under contract, but for standard hosted accounts the guaranteed maximum is 120 days from snapshot creation — meaning deletion requests are guaranteed to have deleted data removed from live systems and queued for backup purging within 30 days; in very rare administrative edge cases the full snapshot TTL may reach 120 days. We will include the 120-day maximum in procurement paperwork if you need the guarantee.

2) Deletion API & derived artifacts
- The Deletion API removes primary request logs, cached generations, and schedules index/vector entries for deletion. Embedded/derived vectors that were materialized into a separate index (for example, if Clearwater used our managed semantic search product) are also removed as part of the same deletion workflow. If a customer exported embeddings to their own storage, Redwood cannot delete those external copies — we will document that in the attestation.

3) Telemetry & monitoring
- Telemetry: by default, lightweight aggregated usage metrics used for product analytics are processed in our analytics cluster; for pinned accounts we can configure telemetry ingestion to remain within the selected region and avoid cross-region exports. Third-party monitoring integrations (e.g., Datadog) are opt-in; if enabled they will send metrics to the third party endpoints you configure and Redwood will not forward telemetry outside the pinned region by default. We will include a template config showing opt-in toggles.
